_README: Measured kernel cycles, consumed by loop/llama_project.py.
Entries with `cycles: null` are PLACEHOLDERS until someone fills them in
from a real Verilator run (the SoC does ~1.8k cycles/s, so only single
kernels are measurable; the whole model is projected, never simulated).
Fields:
kernel         one of the kernel types in loop/llama_model.py
shape          the shape that was actually measured (documentation)
work_metric    'macs' or 'elems' - which quantity cycles scale with
work_measured  value of that metric at the measured shape
cycles         total cycles for one call at that shape (null = not measured)
overhead_cycles  fixed per-call cost (setup, config, fences) subtracted
before linear extrapolation and re-added per call
device         'gemmini' or 'saturn' - which unit ran it
source         where the number came from
Scaling rule applied by llama_project.py:
cycles(target) = calls*overhead + (cycles - overhead) * work_target/work_measured
Entries with cycles == null fall back to roofline x --fallback-factor and
are flagged 'est' in the output tables.
HOW TO SWITCH decode GEMV BETWEEN SATURN AND GEMMINI
project() looks up `<kernel>_<unit>` first when `--device kernel=unit` is
given on the CLI (e.g. `--device int8_gemv=gemmini` -> `int8_gemv_gemmini`),
and falls back to the bare `<kernel>` entry otherwise. An entry's own
`device` field is only used when the CLI did NOT pin that kernel.
The two candidate numbers for the SAME decode GEMV shape (M=512, K=2048,
1,048,576 MACs, 1 MiB of weights) are:
saturn  621724 cycles  (1.69 B/cycle of weights)  <- naive RVV baseline
gemmini 150339 cycles  (6.97 B/cycle of weights)  <- 4.1x faster
So: no --device -> saturn (bare entries); `--device int8_gemv=gemmini
--device lm_head_gemv=gemmini` -> the *_gemmini entries.
WHY MAC-LINEAR SCALING IS OK FOR A DECODE GEMV
At N=1 a GEMV does exactly one MAC per weight byte, so scaling by MACs is
scaling by weight traffic - which is what actually costs cycles here. Do
NOT extrapolate the N=64 `int8_gemm` measurement down to decode: at N=64
the weight mvin is amortized over 64 rows of work, at N=1 over one. That
extrapolation predicted ~9.01M cycles/token, below the 78M memory roofline
for 1.24 GB of weights, i.e. impossible. The measured N=1 rate of
6.97 B/cycle gives ~178M cycles/token instead.
THE SEVEN NON-GEMM OPERATORS (measured 2026-09-05, Saturn)
rmsnorm, rope, attn_scores, softmax, attn_pv, silu_mul and add are now
real Verilator numbers from the `llama-<op>` benchmarks in
repos/saturn/benchmarks/, registered in loop/kernels.py and run with
`loop.py --kernel llama-<op> --baseline-only --config
GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig`. All seven are PRISTINE naive RVV 1.0
baselines (LMUL=1, no unrolling, no reuse) - they were written to be
MEASURED, not optimized, because together they are ~1% of decode cycles.
Every one of them has 2.5x-60x of headroom to its own roofline; see the
`notes` on each Kernel entry in loop/kernels.py for where it is.
dtype: fp32 activations throughout, matching ModelSpec.acc_bytes = 4.
attn_scores and attn_pv are now costed from the **int8 KV cache**
variants (`llama-attn-scores-q8kv`, `llama-attn-pv-q8kv`), which match
ModelSpec's kv_bytes = 1: K/V stored int8 with one fp32 dequant scale
per KV row, q and P still fp32. The fp32-cache measurements of the
identical shape are kept under each entry's additional_measurements.
SURPRISE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING RESULT HERE: the int8 cache is
SLOWER, not faster - 68,571 vs 60,147 for attn_scores (1.14x) and
62,541 vs 44,765 for attn_pv (1.40x). Quartering the cache took the
memory floor from 8,192 to 2,304 cycles, but because q/P stay fp32
every cached byte must be widened int8 -> int32 -> fp32 before it can
be multiplied: two extra 32-bit-destination ops per element, which
raises the ARITHMETIC floor from 8,192 to 24,576. The kernel goes from
perfectly balanced to compute-bound by 10x. On this SoC, at this shape,
quantising only the cache is a losing trade.
That prediction was then TESTED. `llama-attn-scores-int8` and
`llama-attn-pv-int8` quantise the activation side as well (int8 q with a
per-vector scale; int8 probabilities with V's per-row scales folded in,
since a cross-row reduction cannot carry a per-row scale), accumulate in
int32 with vwmul + vwadd.wv, and do exactly one fp32 multiply per output.
Three measurements of the identical 512x64 shape, all equally naive:
variant   cache        activation   attn_scores   attn_pv
int8      int8  32KiB  int8              51,280    22,856
So quantising the cache ALONE loses (1.14x / 1.40x slower than fp32) and
quantising BOTH sides wins (1.17x / 1.96x faster than fp32, and 1.34x /
2.74x faster than cache-only). The arithmetic floors say why:
variant   memory floor   arithmetic floor   binding
fp32             8,192              8,192   balanced
q8kv             2,304             24,576   compute, 10x
int8             2,300              8,192   compute, ~3.6x
int8 activations delete the per-element vsext+vfcvt, putting the
arithmetic floor back where fp32's was while keeping a quarter of the
traffic - the only one of the three with slack on BOTH resources.
Accuracy is not the obstacle: measured relative L2 error against a true
fp32 reference is 1.7e-3 (scores) and 2.9e-3 (pv), 10-17x inside the
3e-2 gate. Each of those kernels also carries an EXACT int32 self-check,
so quantisation tolerance never hides a kernel bug.
The primary cost basis above is still the q8kv (int8 cache, fp32
activation) entry, deliberately: moving the model to full int8 attention
changes the attention CONTRACT (softmax must emit int8 probabilities and
q_proj must emit an int8 query), which is a model decision and not a
kernel optimization. The full-int8 numbers are recorded under each
entry's additional_measurements so the switch can be costed the moment
it is taken: it would move decode from 261.68M to 232.51M cycles/token
(3.82 -> 4.30 tokens/s) and prefill from 16.42M to 14.57M (60.9 -> 68.6).
Both are measured for ONE query head (32,768 MACs); MAC-linear scaling
multiplies them by the 32 heads x 16 layers the profile asks for.
`rope` is ONE measurement covering both rope calls of a layer (rope_q
2048 elems + rope_k 512 elems = 2560); elems-linear scaling splits it.
STILL ESTIMATED (cycles == null -> roofline x --fallback-factor):
embedding     a 2048-byte row gather out of the 128256x2048 table
lm_head_gemm  the prefill output projection (same shape as lm_head_gemv)
In prefill the seven measurements above are extrapolated from their decode
shapes by elems/macs, which is right for the elementwise ops (N tokens is
N times the elements) but optimistic for attn_scores/attn_pv, where the
causal N(N+1)/2 shape is a different kernel, not a longer one.

loop baseline llama-attn-scores-q8kv 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 kernel (44,591 instructions, IPC 0.65); memory floor 2,304 but ARITHMETIC floor 24,576 (int8->int32->fp32 is two extra 32-bit-destination ops per element on top of the FMA), so 2.79x the binding floor. Self-check: all 512 scores vs a scalar dequantise-and-dot reference, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. int8 K cache with a PER-ROW fp32 dequant scale (kv_bytes=1, matching ModelSpec); q stays fp32. ONE query head (32,768 MACs); the projection multiplies by calls=32 heads x 16 layers. NOTE: the fp32-KV measurement of the identical shape is 60,147 cycles — FASTER, see additional_measurements.

additional_measurements.source: loop baseline llama-attn-scores 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 kernel with an **fp32** K cache (35,884 instructions, IPC 0.60); roofline 8,192 (compute and memory exactly balanced), i.e. 7.3x the floor. Self-check: all 512 scores vs a scalar dot product, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. Kept for comparison: the fp32 cache moves 4x the bytes but needs NO int8->fp32 conversion, and on this SoC that makes it 1.14x FASTER than the int8 version above.

loop baseline llama-attn-scores-int8 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 kernel (20,524 instructions, IPC 0.40); FULLY QUANTISED — int8 cache AND int8 query (per-vector scale), int32 accumulation (vwmul + vwadd.wv, the llama-q8-gemv inner loop), one fp32 rescale per output and NO per-element int8->fp32 conversion. Memory floor ~2,300, arithmetic floor 8,192 (int32 accumulate at 4 lanes/cycle), so 6.26x the binding floor. Self-check: all 512 scores EXACT vs a scalar int32 dot over the same bytes (gate A, 1e-4 rel), plus a quantisation gate on the relative L2 distance to a true fp32 reference (gate B, measured 1.7e-3 against a 3e-2 budget), PASSED. THE COMPARISON: fp32 cache+fp32 act = 60,147, int8 cache+fp32 act = 68,571, int8 cache+int8 act = 51,280 — quantising the cache ALONE loses, quantising both sides wins (1.17x faster than fp32, 1.34x faster than cache-only). NOT the primary cost basis: the model is still costed from the int8-KV/fp32-activation entry above, because switching to full int8 attention is a change to the attention contract, not a kernel optimization.

entries.source: loop baseline llama-attn-pv-q8kv 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 kernel (46,632 instructions, IPC 0.75); memory floor 2,304 but ARITHMETIC floor 24,576 (int8->int32->fp32 is two extra 32-bit-destination ops per element on top of the FMA), so 2.54x the binding floor. Self-check: all 64 outputs vs a scalar dequantise-and-reduce reference, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. int8 V cache with a PER-ROW fp32 dequant scale (kv_bytes=1, matching ModelSpec); P stays fp32 and the scale folds into the row's scalar multiplier. ONE query head (32,768 MACs); the projection multiplies by calls=32 heads x 16 layers. NOTE: the fp32-KV measurement of the identical shape is 44,765 cycles — FASTER, see additional_measurements.

Self-check: all 64 outputs vs a scalar reduction over the 512 rows, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. Kept for comparison: 1.40x FASTER than the int8 version above.

loop baseline llama-attn-pv-int8 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 kernel (16,877 instructions, IPC 0.74); FULLY QUANTISED — int8 cache AND int8 probabilities (single scale, with V's per-row scales folded in), int32 accumulation (vwmul + vwadd.wv, the llama-q8-gemv inner loop), one fp32 rescale per output and NO per-element int8->fp32 conversion. Memory floor ~2,300, arithmetic floor 8,192 (int32 accumulate at 4 lanes/cycle), so 2.79x the binding floor. Self-check: all 64 outputs EXACT vs a scalar int32 accumulation over the same bytes (gate A, 1e-4 rel), plus a quantisation gate on the relative L2 distance to a true fp32 reference (gate B, measured 2.9e-3 against a 3e-2 budget), PASSED. THE COMPARISON: fp32 cache+fp32 act = 44,765, int8 cache+fp32 act = 62,541, int8 cache+int8 act = 22,856 — quantising the cache ALONE loses, quantising both sides wins (1.96x faster than fp32, 2.74x faster than cache-only). NOT the primary cost basis: the model is still costed from the int8-KV/fp32-activation entry above, because switching to full int8 attention is a change to the attention contract, not a kernel optimization.

entries.source: loop baseline llama-rmsnorm 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 fp32 kernel (3,896 instructions, IPC 0.71); roofline 1,536, i.e. 3.6x the floor. Self-check: all 2048 outputs vs a scalar double-precision reference, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. fp32 activations, as ModelSpec.acc_bytes=4 assumes.

loop baseline llama-rope 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 fp32 kernel (3,565 instructions, IPC 0.76); roofline 1,280, i.e. 3.7x the floor. Self-check: all 2560 rotated elements vs a scalar reference, 1e-4 relative, PASSED. ONE measurement covering BOTH rope calls of a layer (rope_q 2048 elems + rope_k 512 elems = 2560); elems-linear scaling splits it back correctly. cos/sin table is an input (precomputed once per position), not part of the kernel.

loop baseline llama-softmax 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 fp32 kernel (3,236 instructions, IPC 0.15); roofline 2,560, i.e. 8.6x the floor. Self-check: all 512 outputs vs a scalar libm expf reference, 1e-4 relative, output sum = 1.0, PASSED. ONE head's 512-long score row; the projection multiplies by 32 heads x 16 layers. IPC 0.15: a 512-element row is mostly a long dependent Cephes-exp chain at a 2-beat chime plus a full-precision vfdiv. Roofline 2560 assumes ~18 flop/elem for the exponential, so it MOVES if a cheaper exp is used.

loop baseline llama-silu-mul 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 fp32 kernel (48,180 instructions, IPC 0.13); roofline 6,144, i.e. 58.8x the floor. Self-check: 512 sampled outputs (stride 13, wrapping) vs a scalar libm reference, 1e-4 relative, plus a checksum over all 8192, PASSED. By far the most expensive elementwise op and the one with the most headroom: 6144 is the MEMORY floor, the arithmetic floor of this Cephes-exp + vfdiv formulation is ~45,000, and the measurement is ~8x THAT. IPC 0.13 = dependent polynomial chain at LMUL=1 plus a serialising divide.

loop baseline llama-add 2026-09-05 GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig Verilator, --baseline-only, pristine naive RVV 1.0 fp32 kernel (2,840 instructions, IPC 0.72); roofline 1,536, i.e. 2.6x the floor. Self-check: all 2048 outputs BIT-EXACT against x0[i]+y[i] (a single fp32 add has one correct answer), PASSED. Pure memory traffic: 24 KiB moved, no reassociation possible.
